fieldData.full-article-text:
For a validator node, based on our initial testing, we currently recommend the equivalent of an AWS c5.xlarge instance provisioned with a gp2 storage volume - with an upper bound of 500 GB for the duration of betanet. We have found this configuration to keep up with consensus without bottlenecking; and it stores ledger state sufficiently to correctly participate in consensus if connected to a fast, reliable internet connection. This is the equivalent of a relatively small virtual server with 4 cores, 8GB of memory, and an SSD. Note that as we learn more about true practical demands during betanet and following mainnet launch, this recommendation may change.

For a full node, a regular home PC should be sufficient with similar storage capacity, although cloud hosting is the typical choice.

Running in archive mode requires the node to store a large amount of indexing data that is needed to provide the JSON-RPC API for clients. This means that storage capacity requirements may be multiple times that of a full/validator node.

For more information on running a node, please visit docs.radixdlt.com.
